newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurd group abandons dam attack, flees town.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group abandons dam attack, flees town.

text.p: Pro-Baghdad Iraqi Kurdish guerrillas on Monday withdrew from a town in northern Iraq and abandoned an assault on a strategic dam under heavy artillery fire from a rival militia, witnesses said.

Thousands of Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) fighters fled the Dukan Dam in a fleet of buses, minibuses and other vehicles. Shells fired from Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) forces defending the dam exploded 100 metres (yards) behind them.
Many of the vehicles ferried the bodies of dead KDP fighters from the front. Massoud Barzani's KDP also fled the town of Ranya, which it took from the PUK of Jalal Talabani only at the weekend.
"We came across very heavy resistence and we are evaluating the situation," local KDP commander Abduljelil Seili told Reuters minutes before he and his men abandoned Ranya.
Shopkeepers closed their shutters and residents ran for the shelter of home ahead of an expected PUK advance.
The fighting took place amid the start to a fresh U.S. peace bid. An envoy from Washington held talks with Barzani in Turkey on Monday, with talks with the PUK set for Tuesday.
